status: PREREGISTERED - committed before any measured run; everything run before this commit is shakedown and is reported as such
question: Can 3-4 Hermes + cua-driver agents run concurrently on one machine, each on its own fixture instance, without cross-agent interference, and what does concurrency buy over running them one at a time? (kvnloo/cua#36-relevant multi-session evidence; compositor is headless sway, not Hyprland; kvnloo/cua#94 stays separate.)
scope_guard: kvnloo/hermes-agent#319 directive: no new integration architecture, protocol, question family or active controller. No Hermes or Driver code change. Shadow/observer output never reaches Hermes (offline only). Hermes is the executor; success is judged only by the independent fixture oracle; no observer or agent self-credits success. CUA invariants (kvnloo/cua#73/#93): no new Driver services, fresh verification retained, no blind replay.

topology.chosen: one private headless sway 1.12 instance per agent (cua-sway-session.sh, CUA_SWAY_SEATS=1, 1280x800, private AT-SPI), N = 4 sessions at once
topology.why_not_single_compositor_multiseat: cua-driver 0.32.0 has no seat selection: SOURCE wayland/primary_seat.rs Seats::selected() takes the last advertised wl_seat; REAL (sway setup packet) every Driver event landed on seat1 of a 2-seat sway; the Driver's X11 path injects inside Xwayland, below sway's seats. Orchestrator decision 4: report single-compositor multi-seat Driver use as BLOCKED; replicated here as control SD.
topology.why_sway_not_xvfb: the sway kit passed its isolation canary (3/3) and is the compositor the spec names; Xvfb (cua-x11-session.sh) is the fallback only if sway sessions fail readiness
topology.per_session: fixture (upstream CuaTestHarness GTK3 TaskWindow, unmodified, as an X11 client of the session's private Xwayland, wrapped by harness/journaled_fixture.py which only adds an app-side append-only journal) + one Hermes process + the cua-driver MCP child Hermes spawns
topology.shared: one model server (Ollama 0.35.0 on 127.0.0.1:11500, started by another stack lane; observed 2 slots x 32768 ctx; also serving other lanes' requests), CPU, RAM, GPU
topology.look_alike_property: all instances have the same window title; because each session has its own PID namespace and X server, the fixture is pid 59 and the X window id 4194308 in every session (observed in shakedown), so identical (pid, window_id) handles name different windows

declared_config_and_harness_choices: Hermes config (private HERMES_HOME per agent): custom provider -> 127.0.0.1:11500/v1, observer plugin on (metadata only), updates/catalog/telemetry off, computer_use.permission_mode standard, native_wayland false.

tools.tool_search.defer = the product default list minus computer_use, so computer_use is an eager tool. Shakedown: with the default the 3B and 7B models had to reach computer_use through the tool_call bridge and failed (5/5 malformed bridge calls).

Approvals: no --yolo, no approvals.mode change, no bypass variable. command_allowlist holds the exact computer_use scopes the task needs (cua:click/type/key foreground+background, double_click/set_value/focus_app/scroll background) - the product's own permanent-grant mechanism (what an operator's 'always' answer writes). bring_to_front, drag, right/middle click stay ungranted.

Fixture window server-side border removed with a runtime per-window swaymsg command. Shakedown: with sway's title bar the Driver's AT-SPI element bounds and its window-local click frame differ by the decoration offset (+2, +27 px), so clicks at element centres miss (hermes-7b-3..5).

Pointer warm-up before each agent: xdotool motion only (two moves in blank window area, no button, no key). Shakedown: without it the first XTEST click the Driver sends into a fresh Xwayland is dropped (fgtype-3: 3 clicks -> counter 2; fgtype-4 with warm-up: 3 -> 3).

Prompt (identical across arms except the token): fixed 6-step procedure, text-only capture (mode=ax), coordinate clicks with delivery_mode=foreground, 'never pass the element argument'. Reason: Hermes (this stack and upstream main 5bba024d) always sends element_index on element clicks and cua-driver 0.32.0 (and upstream main 352507b6) refuses it ('click: unknown argument element_index', invalid_arguments) - every element-index click fails; recorded per run as element_index_refusals.

Task: type the agent's unique token into Note and click Save note once. The shakedown's richer task (plus Increment xK) gave 0/16 strict successes across the prompt iterations (hermes-7b-1..16; model confusion between controls), which would leave interference barely measurable; the simplified task gave 3/4 single-agent (hermes-7b-17..20) and 0/4 in one 4-agent concurrent shakedown (conc4-1).
Max 16 turns per agent, 900 s agent timeout, 1200 s session timeout.

M_main.what: 8 round pairs; each pair = one SEQ round (agents A1..A4 one after another, each in a fresh session) and one CONC round (A1..A4 at the same time, one session each); order seq-first in odd pairs, conc-first in even pairs

L_lookalike.what: 5 rounds of 2 concurrent agents, identical prompts except the token, look-alike windows (same title, same pid, same X window id)

X_crosswire.what: 3 reps: session A (attacker) makes deliberate cross-session attempts against session B's idle look-alike fixture using B's published addresses: C0 own fill (sanity); X1 B's X display by number; X2 B's X socket by backing path (Driver); X3 same via xdotool/libX11; X4 raw X11 connection setup on B's backing path (reachability only); D1 own X display + B's D-Bus/AT-SPI bus by backing path (Driver); W1 B's Wayland socket by path (seatctl pointer+keyboard); S1 B's sway IPC by path (read-only get_version)

SL_seat_lookalike.what: 3 reps in ONE 2-seat sway: two seatprobe windows with the same title; seat0 and seat1 concurrently click + type a seat-specific token into the left/right window, then swap (non-Driver: seatctl)

SD_seat_driver.what: 2 reps in ONE 2-seat sway: two concurrent cua-driver processes (agent A -> left window, agent B -> right window), native Wayland arm, foreground pixel clicks

oracle.primary: fixture journals (written by the app itself: every state publish, every Note text change, every focus change) and the final fixture state file; never the model's text, never Driver success messages
oracle.secondary: per-session sway get_tree/get_seats before/after (foreign views, focused view); seatprobe per-seat event logs (the compositor names the seat of every event)
oracle.diagnostic_only: lane-private Hermes transcript (stale-ref / refusal / element_index refusal counts), observer spool (API calls, prompt_tokens), shared server log (requests in the round window, to count other lanes' requests)
oracle.success_definition: final note_saved == the agent's own token AND no other agent's token anywhere in its journal AND counter/agreed/size untouched

per_agent: foreign views in its session after the run
interference: cross-session landings = any token of agent i found in the journal of agent j != i (all rounds, all journals)
focus stolen (focused view after != own fixture, or unpaired focus-out)
throughput: round makespan; per-pair speedup = seq makespan / conc makespan
successes per minute and agent runs per minute per arm
own model-call overlap seconds (do concurrent agents actually overlap at the model)
resources: CPU % (mean over the round) and peak RSS of the round's process tree and of each session
GPU memory used (peak, mean) and utilisation (nvidia-smi, 1 Hz)
metrics.contamination: requests on the shared model server in the round window minus this round's own API calls = other lanes' requests (model_requests_foreign)

hypotheses_and_gates.H1_isolation_primary: 0 cross-session landings across all M and L journals (74 agent runs). GATE: one landing fails the no-interference claim.
hypotheses_and_gates.H2_windows_focus: every session tree after a run holds only its own fixture view, and its focused view is its own fixture (where the fixture is alive). GATE: one foreign view or foreign focus fails the claim.
hypotheses_and_gates.H3_throughput: CONC makespan < SEQ makespan (speedup > 1) in >= 6 of 8 pairs; median speedup reported with min/max. Expected well below 4x: the shared model server has 2 slots and also serves other lanes.
hypotheses_and_gates.H4_success_parity: descriptive: success rate CONC vs SEQ with Wilson 95% intervals and the difference; no equivalence claim at n = 32 per arm.
hypotheses_and_gates.H5_stale_and_duplicates: descriptive: stale-ref results and duplicate effects per run, CONC vs SEQ.

HX_crosswire_predictions.X2: no landing (Driver cannot open a path display)
HX_crosswire_predictions.X3: no landing (libX11 path display not accepted)
HX_crosswire_predictions.X4: connection accepted at protocol level (the backing X socket is a same-uid path socket)
HX_crosswire_predictions.D1: lands in B (AT-SPI over B's bus; pid 59 names B's fixture there)

hypotheses_and_gates.HX_gate: if any of X4/D1/W1/S1 reaches B, the isolation claim is bounded to 'agents that only know their own session's addresses never interfere'; sibling sessions of the same uid are NOT isolated against a deliberately cross-wired client (path sockets under the session run dirs are reachable). The oracle must detect every landing that happens (sensitivity: C0 and any landing attempt must show up in the right journal).
hypotheses_and_gates.HSL: 3/3 reps: each window receives exactly the tokens of the seat that targeted it, 0 cross-seat landings (non-Driver)
hypotheses_and_gates.HSD: 2/2 reps: both Driver agents' events arrive on the same seat (no per-agent seat binding) -> single-compositor multi-seat Driver use BLOCKED

analysis.denominators: every launched agent run counts; a crashed session, non-zero rc, missing journal or timeout is a failure (success = false) and stays in the denominator; no run is dropped or re-run
analysis.contamination: all rounds reported; rounds with model_requests_foreign > 0 are flagged; throughput is reported for all pairs and, as a sensitivity row, for pairs where both rounds had no foreign requests (if any exist)
analysis.timing_source: round makespan = run_round.sh wall clock inside quiet-timed; ledger lines ms-main-* are the lock receipts

claim_boundary: Compositor: headless sway 1.12 (wlroots 0.20, pixman), X11 fixture via Xwayland. Not Hyprland/Omarchy (#94 separate), not a physical seat, not Chromium/browser sessions (#36's browser row was covered upstream by trycua/cua#4317).
One fixture type, one task, text-only AX capture, one shared local 7B executor; success rates measure this executor + stack, not the Driver alone.
Single-compositor multi-seat with the Driver is BLOCKED (no seat selection); the multi-agent result is N separate compositors.
Throughput numbers are for this machine under concurrent load from other lanes, with a shared 2-slot model server; they are not a capacity benchmark.
Isolation evidence covers agents that only know their own session; cross-session reachability by a deliberately cross-wired same-uid client is measured separately (X runs).
